Choosing a color in Color Flip’s ten-step trail

Use the named target and four labeled swatches in current Color Flip; learn when the active color stays put or cycles after a submission.

By NoCharge·Reviewed by NoCharge·Published August 15, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Pick a color. Step carefully. Take your time.

Play Color FlipBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: Current Color Flip is a ten-answer color-matching session, not a tile-boundary or movement puzzle. Read the next named target, choose a swatch, and submit it.

Read the target, not a location

The target trail has ten numbered positions and names the next color in text. The four available swatches are Coral, Teal, Gold, and Violet. There is no 5×5 board, adjacent tile, direction key, or timing window to hit.

Choose and submit

Tap or activate one of the labeled swatches, then choose Lock color and continue. The score increases only when the selected color matches the current target. A miss does not end the session; you can continue through all ten positions and see the final total.

When the active swatch changes

In Trail session, the selected color stays active by default. You can advance it manually with Cycle color or turn on Rotate palette to move to the next color after each submission. In Color cycle mode, the active swatch advances automatically after each lock. The order is Coral, Teal, Gold, Violet, then Coral again.

The current target trail and palette are deterministic, and reset restores the same sequence. There is no countdown or saved local-best record. For a detailed explanation of the palette behavior, read How Color Flip’s palette cycle works.
